chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman whose husband was absent; he returned while she was performing i'tikaf (spiritual retreat) in the mosque with his permission. She left the mosque upon hearing of his arrival and went to her house, preparing for her husband until they consummated the marriage. He said: If she left the mosque before three days had passed and she had not stipulated in her i'tikaf [that leaving for her husband does not break it], then she bears the same ruling as the one who performs kaffarat al-zhihar (expiation for zhihar).

key_terms.اعْتِكَافٌ: I'tikaf: Spiritual retreat in a mosque
key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: Al-Muzahhir: One who performs zhihar (declaring his wife like his mother's back)
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ زَوْجِهَا: With the permission of her husband
key_terms.مَا عَلَى الْمُظَاهِرِ: The ruling of the one who performs zhihar (referring to the expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who breaks her i'tikaf to have marital relations with her husband?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of i'tikaf (spiritual retreat), where the woman's departure to consummate the marriage is treated as a breach of the sanctity of the mosque. The specific penalty of kaffarat al-zhihar (expiation for zhihar) is applied because the act of intimacy occurred within the sacred precincts, mirroring the legal consequences of declaring one's wife unlawful through zhihar. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the physical location of the act determines the specific expiation required for the violation.
